The run\n+executes the seed scenario suite across a vendor allowlist (default `claude` + `codex`),\n+appends results to a durable store, writes review findings, and emits capability gaps\n+(`source:scenario-parity`) that `/improve-harness` reads. It is **off by default** and ships\n+only as templates: nothing in the repository installs, enables or starts a schedule.\n+\n+## Install (operator, once)\n+\n+1. Create a **dedicated nightly user/HOME** on the host. It must have: no user-global skills\n+   (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`), no coordinator MCP configuration, and no GitHub\n+   push credentials (SSH keys, credential helpers, `insteadOf` rewrites). Vendor CLIs keep\n+   their own auth under that HOME, so these are controlled operationally; the executor\n+   cannot replace HOME. Install the `claude` and `codex` CLIs and their keys for that user.\n+2. Copy `packages/agent-scenarios/deploy/nightly.example.yaml` to\n+   `~/.config/agent-scenarios/nightly.yaml`, fill `vendor_commands` and the paths, and keep\n+   `enabled: false`.\n+3. Review the plan: `agent-scenarios nightly --dry-run`. It prints the off-switch state, the\n+   effective vendors, the planned (scenario, vendor) pairs and the cap evaluation; it takes no\n+   lock, writes no record and starts no vendor (it works with `enabled: false`).\n+4. Render the unit and timer from `deploy/systemd/*.template` (replace `@UV@` and `@REPO@`),\n+   place them in `~/.config/systemd/user/`, run `systemctl --user daemon-reload`. Keep\n+   `TimeoutStartSec` at or above `max_wall_clock_minutes + per_pair_timeout_seconds + 10 min`\n+   (default 270 min): the budget is only checked between pairs.\n+5. Flip `enabled: true`, run the service once by hand, review results/findings/gaps, then\n+   `systemctl --user enable --now agent-scenarios-nightly.timer`.\n+\n+## Disable (any one of)\n+\n+- `systemctl --user disable --now agent-scenarios-nightly.timer`\n+- create the kill-file (`disable_file`, default `~/.config/agent-scenarios/DISABLED`)\n+- set `enabled: false`\n+\n+A disabled run appends a `disabled` run record, constructs no executor and exits 0.\n+\n+## Exit codes and triage\n+\n+| Code | Meaning | First action |\n+|------|---------|--------------|\n+| 0 | `completed`, every pair passed (also `disabled` / `locked`) | none |\n+| 1 | one or more scenarios `fail` | `results query --status fail`; a capability gap was emitted per failing (scenario, vendor) |\n+| 2 | config or cap error (invalid config writes **no** record; `cap_exceeded`, `config_error` write one) | fix the config or raise the cap deliberately; nothing was launched |\n+| 3 | no `fail`, but one or more `error` results (a CLI missing, expired keys, timeouts, an unsupported `gh` call) **or** an incomplete matrix (`budget_exhausted`) | read the `error` text in `results query --status error`; no capability gap is emitted for infrastructure errors |\n+\n+Precedence: 2 > 1 > 3 > 0. Systemd marks the unit failed for 1, 2 and 3 (`SuccessExitStatus=0`).\n+Error texts: `vendor CLI timed out after Ns` (raise `per_pair_timeout_seconds` or investigate\n+the scenario) is distinct from `vendor CLI unavailable` (binary missing);\n+`gh shim: unsupported call ...` means the agent used a `gh` subcommand the local shim does\n+not implement (widen the shim in a follow-up change; it is not a skill failure).\n+\n+## Hermetic live runs\n+\n+Each pair runs in `<workspaces_root>/<run_id>/<scenario>--<vendor>/` against a fixture-local\n+bare `origin` (`<workspace>.origin.git`). `gh` resolves to a local shim (`<workspace>.bin/gh`)\n+so no call reaches GitHub. The vendor subprocess never sees GitHub tokens, any coordinator\n+URL / API key / Cloudflare Access variable, or the variables named by `gaps.api_key_env` /\n+`gaps.coordinator_url_env`, and `COORDINATION_API_URL` is forced to `http://127.0.0.1:9`.\n+`env_scrub` can only add to that denylist and `env_set` may not name any scrubbed variable.\n+The whole `skills/` tree of the checkout under test is copied into the workspace's\n+`.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` (excluded from git) and `skills_sha` (`+dirty` when\n+modified) is recorded on every result.\n+\n+## Workspaces and retention\n+\n+Workspaces of `pass` and `skipped_budget` pairs are deleted after scoring; `fail` and `error`\n+workspaces (and their `.origin.git`) are kept for diagnosis. At the start of each run, run\n+directories beyond the newest `retain_failed_runs` (default 7) are deleted.\n+\n+## Results\n+\n+```\n+agent-scenarios results query  --vendor codex --skill validate-feature --since 2026-10-01\n+agent-scenarios results query  --family merge --status fail --format table\n+agent-scenarios results trend  --group-by vendor,skill --bucket week\n+agent-scenarios results latest --skill implement-feature\n+```\n+\n+Records are appended as each pair is scored, so a killed run keeps its completed pairs; a\n+`result` whose `run_id` has no `run` record is reported as `interrupted` (or `in_progress`\n+while the run lock is held). Trend pass rate is `pass / (pass + fail)`; `error` and\n+`skipped_budget` are counted separately.\n+\n+## Capability gaps and /improve-harness\n+\n+Each deterministic `fail` becomes one memory entry tagged `source:scenario-parity` (see\n+`docs/guides/memory-conventions.md`). Undeliverable entries are spooled to `gap-spool.jsonl`\n+and replayed at the start of the next run or by `agent-scenarios gaps flush`; delivery counts\n+only on HTTP 2xx with `success: true`, and an unset URL variable spools without any request.\n+\n+- **Frequency unit**: `/improve-harness` counts raw memory entries, so a finding's frequency\n+  is the number of failing **(run, vendor) pairs**, not nights.\n+- **Two URL variables, one coordinator**: the gap emitter reads `COORDINATION_API_URL`\n+  (default; configurable via `gaps.coordinator_url_env`) and `COORDINATION_API_KEY`, whereas\n+  `/improve-harness` reads `COORDINATOR_URL`. Both must name the same coordinator or the\n+  emitted gaps are never read.\n+- **agent_id must match**: the coordinator filters memory queries on `agent_id` exactly.\n+  Gaps are written as `gaps.agent_id` (default `agent-scenarios-nightly`), and\n+  `/improve-harness` queries `improve-harness` and `agent-scenarios-nightly` by default. If you\n+  change `gaps.agent_id`, set `IMPROVE_HARNESS_AGENT_ID` (comma-separated) to include it; an\n+  API key bound to a single agent can only read that agent's entries.\n+\n+## Broken-skill drill (operator)\n+\n+On a throwaway branch break one plan or validate skill, point a one-off config's `repo_root`\n+at it, run the nightly once, and confirm a `fail` result, a `source:scenario-parity` gap in\n+`/improve-harness`, and that restoring the skill goes green again.\ndiff --git a/docs/guides/memory-conventions.md b/docs/guides/memory-conventions.md\nindex 0f948504..442ce3d3 100644\n--- a/docs/guides/memory-conventions.md\n+++ b/docs/guides/memory-conventions.md\n@@ -12,7 +12,9 @@ All capability-gap entries use the `prefix:value` format:\n | `capability_gap` | Free text | Describes what capability was missing from the harness |\n | `affected_skill` | Skill name (kebab-case) | Which skill was impacted |\n | `severity` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` | Impact severity |\n-| `source` | `self-reported`, `coordinator-emitted`, `session-log`, `transcript-mined` | Which emitter produced this signal |\n+| `source` | `self-reported`, `coordinator-emitted`, `session-log`, `transcript-mined`, `scenario-parity` | Which emitter produced this signal |\n+| `vendor` | Vendor id (`claude`, `codex`, ...) | Auxiliary; b/openspec/changes/seed-scenario-suite-and-nightly-cross-vendor-parity-runs/design.md\n@@ -0,0 +1,538 @@\n+# Design: Seed scenario suite and nightly cross-vendor parity runs\n+\n+## Context\n+\n+ri-15 (`build-agent-trajectory-scenario-harness`) built the harness library in\n+`packages/agent-scenarios/`. Its learnings that constrain this design:\n+\n+- The **deterministic goal-gate scorer is authoritative**; the LLM judge is additive\n+  and skip-never-fail. Nothing in this change lets a judge verdict create a\n+  capability gap or change a pass/fail.\n+- `command` gates resolve `python` to `sys.executable`.\n+- Live multi-vendor runs happen on the **GX10** with real CLIs; in-container and CI\n+  tests use `FakeExecutor`.\n+- `run_scenario` already distinguishes `deterministic_status` `pass | fail | error`,\n+  where `error` means the executor (CLI missing, non-zero exit, fixture failure)\n+  failed — that is infrastructure, not skill quality.\n+\n+Data flow after this change:\n+\n+```\n+nightly config ──► nightly.run()\n+                     │ 1. off-switch / kill-file / run lock\n+                     │ 2. flush gap spool (previous offline run)\n+                     │ 3. load suite, apply vendor allowlist, plan pairs\n+                     │ 4. cap check (max_pairs, per-vendor) — refuse if over\n+                     │ 5. run pairs (CLIVendorExecutor, skills_root, env scrub,\n+                     │    wall-clock budget → remaining pairs skipped_budget)\n+                     ├──► results_store.append(records)        (JSONL, trend)\n+                     ├──► findings_emitter.emit_findings(...)  (review-findings JSON)\n+                     └──► gap_emitter.emit(fail verdicts)      (memory API | spool)\n+                                          │\n+                       /improve-harness ◄─┘ (POST /memory/query, source:scenario-parity)\n+```\n+\n+## Decisions\n+\n+### D1 — Package-local runner and stores (Approach 1)\n+\n+All new runtime code lives in `packages/agent-scenarios/` as library modules with\n+thin CLI subcommands. Rationale and rejected alternatives are in `proposal.md`\n+(Approaches Considered). The coordinator is only a *consumer-facing sink* for\n+capability gaps through an endpoint that already exists (`POST /memory/store`).\n+\n+### D2 — Results store: append-only JSONL behind a `ResultsStore` interface\n+\n+**Choice**: one JSONL file (default `$XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-scenarios/results.jsonl`,\n+override via config `results.path` or `--store`). Two record types, both carrying\n+`schema_version: 1` and `record_type`:\n+\n+- `result` — one per (run_id, scenario_id, vendor): `recorded_at`, `run_id`,\n+  `scenario_id`, `skill_under_test`, `skill_family`, `vendor`,\n+  `deterministic_status` (`pass | fail | error | skipped_budget`), `failed_gates`\n+  (ids), `trajectory_status`, `duration_seconds`, `repo_sha`, `skills_sha`, `error`.\n+- `run` — one per nightly invocation: `run_id`, `started_at`, `finished_at`,\n+  `status` (`completed | disabled | cap_exceeded | budget_exhausted | locked |\n+  config_error`), `planned_pairs`, `executed_pairs`, `config_digest`, `vendors`,\n+  `repo_sha`, `skills_sha`, `reason`.\n+\n+Every listed field is present on every record (nullable fields as explicit `null`);\n+the schema also rejects contradictory states (`fail` with no failed gate, `pass` /\n+`skipped_budget` with failed gates, `error` without an `error` message).\n+\n+**Field mapping from ri-15 types** (verified against `models.py`; ri-15's\n+`VendorRunVerdict` has neither a duration nor a flat trajectory status):\n+`failed_gates` = `[g.gate_id for g in verdict.failed_gates]` (gates whose status is\n+`fail` or `error`, in scenario declaration order); `trajectory_status` =\n+`verdict.trajectory.status`; `duration_seconds` is measured by the nightly runner with\n+a monotonic clock around each single-vendor `run_scenario` call; `error` =\n+`verdict.error`. `skipped_budget` records carry `failed_gates: []`,\n+`duration_seconds: null`.\n+\n+**Incremental append**: the nightly runner appends each `result` record as soon as\n+its pair is scored, and the `run` record last. A run killed mid-way (systemd\n+`TimeoutStartSec`, SIGKILL, host reboot) therefore keeps every completed pair's\n+result; `result` records whose `run_id` has no `run` record are reported by\n+`results query`/`trend` as belonging to an *interrupted* run and are otherwise\n+counted normally — unless the run still holds the nightly run lock (a non-blocking\n+`flock` probe of `<state>/nightly.lock`), in which case they are reported as\n+*in progress*, so a query during the nightly window does not mislabel the live run.\n+\n+**Why not SQLite**: SQLite would also work, but at ~12k records/year a full scan is\n+cheap; JSONL is append-only by construction (no in-place updates, no migrations),\n+diffable, greppable, trivially rotated/backed up, and readers can tolerate partial\n+last lines from a crash. **Why not a coordinator table**: no cross-host consumer\n+exists yet; a migration + API + throwaway-DB tests is disproportionate for a\n+single-writer dataset (gatekeeper guidance: simplest durable store). The\n+`ResultsStore` protocol (`append(records)`, `iter_records(filters)`) leaves room for a\n+coordinator-backed implementation later.\n+\n+**Write safety**: appends take an exclusive `fcntl.flock` on the store file and write\n+whole lines with a trailing newline in one `write` + `fsync`; readers skip a\n+trailing partial line and records with an unknown `schema_version` (warning, not\n+error).\n+\n+**Queries** (`agent-scenarios results ...`):\n+- `query --vendor V --skill S --family F --scenario ID --since ISO --until ISO\n+  [--status ...] [--format json|table]` — raw matching `result` records.\n+- `trend --group-by vendor,skill|vendor,family|scenario,vendor --bucket day|week\n+  [filters]` — pass rate, counts per bucket (errors and `skipped_budget` reported\n+  separately and excluded from the pass-rate denominator).\n+- `latest [filters]` — most recent result per (scenario, vendor); the signal a\n+  future dispatcher gate would read.\n+\n+### D3 — Capability-gap emission: `source:scenario-parity` via the memory API, spool fallback\n+\n+For every `VendorRunVerdict` with `deterministic_status == \"fail\"` the gap emitter\n+builds one entry:\n+\n+```\n+event_type: \"capability_gap\"\n+summary:    \"[<vendor>] scenario <scenario_id> failed gates: <gate ids>\"\n+session_id: \"<run_id>\"\n+details:    {run_id, scenario_id, vendor, failed_gates:[{gate_id, detail}], skills_sha, repo_sha}\n+tags:\n+  - capability_gap                              # bare tag: what analyze_failures queries\n+  - capability_gap:scenario-parity/<scenario_id>/<first failed gate id>\n+  - failure_type:verification_failed\n+  - affected_skill:<skill_under_test>\n+  - severity:high\n+  - source:scenario-parity\n+  - vendor:<vendor>\n+  - scenario:<scenario_id>\n+```\n+\n+Notes:\n+- **Bare `capability_gap` tag**: `analyze_failures.query_memory` posts\n+  `tags: [\"capability_gap\"]` and the coordinator's recall matches tags by exact array\n+  overlap (`tags && p_tags`), so a prefixed tag alone would not be returned. Adding\n+  the bare tag is harmless to `_extract_tag` (it only reads `prefix:`-tags).\n+- **Stable `capability_gap` value** (`scenario-parity/<scenario>/<gate>`) so\n+  `/improve-harness` groups repeated nightly failures of the same gate into one\n+  finding whose frequency rises with repeated failures. `<gate>` is the first failed\n+  gate in **scenario declaration order** (not verdict order), so the key is stable.\n+- **Frequency unit is (run, vendor), not nights.** `/improve-harness` ranks raw\n+  memory entries (`rank_findings` counts entries per `capability_gap` value; its\n+  `deduplicate_findings` result is discarded — a known consumer bug owned by a\n+  separate change), and `POST /memory/query` does not return `session_id`. So two\n+  vendors failing the same gate in one run contribute frequency 2. This change does\n+  **not** repair the consumer's ranking; it documents the unit (runbook, memory\n+  conventions) and carries `run_id` inside `details` so a later consumer fix can\n+  collapse per run. The consumer test pins the actual behaviour: two vendors in one\n+  run → 2, plus a later run → 3.\n+- **Detail bound**: each `failed_gates[].detail` is truncated to 500 characters\n+  (also encoded as `maxLength: 500` in the contract), so a command gate's captured\n+  output cannot bloat memory or carry large log excerpts.\n+- **Only `fail` emits gaps.** `error` (CLI missing, timeout, fixture failure) and\n+  `skipped_budget` are infrastructure outcomes: recorded in the results store and the\n+  run summary, never as skill capability gaps. Judge findings never emit gaps (D3 of\n+  ri-15: judge is additive).\n+- **Severity `high`** for every deterministic failure (gates are explicit contract\n+  violations); not `critical`, which the D4 schema reserves for incidents.\n+- **Sinks** (`MemorySink` protocol): `CoordinatorMemorySink` — stdlib `urllib` POST to\n+  `${COORDINATION_API_URL}/memory/store` with `Authorization: Bearer ${COORDINATION_API_KEY}`\n+  (the coordinator's preferred header; `X-API-Key` is its legacy alias)\n+  (variable names configurable via `gaps.coordinator_url_env` / `gaps.api_key_env`;\n+  the defaults follow the repo-wide convention in\n+  `docs/coordination-detection-template.md`, whereas `analyze_failures.py` reads\n+  `COORDINATOR_URL` — the runbook requires both to name the same coordinator), a 10 s\n+  request timeout, and `agent_id` from config (default `agent-scenarios-nightly`).\n+  An unset URL variable means \"spool everything\" (no localhost fallback, so a\n+  misconfigured host never writes to an unintended coordinator). **Delivery is\n+  acknowledged only by HTTP 2xx with a JSON body whose `success` is `true`**; a 200\n+  with `success: false`, a non-JSON body, or any other status is a failed delivery\n+  and the entry is spooled (on emit) or kept (on flush). `SpoolMemorySink` —\n+  appends the identical payload to `<state>/gap-spool.jsonl`. The emitter tries the\n+  coordinator and spools any entry that fails. `agent-scenarios gaps flush` (also run\n+  at the start of every nightly) replays the spool and rewrites it with only the\n+  entries that still failed. No dependency on `skills/coordination-bridge` (the\n+  package must stay installable on its own).\n+- **Base-spec enum**: `openspec/specs/harness-engineering/spec.md` \"Capability Gap\n+  Detection\" still lists a closed four-value `source` enum, and the in-flight\n+  `add-a-judged-first-stage-to-coordinator-audit-triage` MODIFIES that requirement.\n+  The ADDED requirement here states that it extends that enum; whichever of the two\n+  changes archives second reconciles the enum text (adds `scenario-parity` to the\n+  MODIFIED copy, or files a follow-up MODIFIED delta) — tracked as task 6.4.\n+- **Shared tag schema**: `source:scenario-parity` is a *new vocabulary value*. It is\n+  documented in `docs/guides/memory-conventions.md` and added to the\n+  `SOURCE_VOCABULARY` constant in `skills/session-log/tests/test_memory_tag_conventions.py`\n+  (the doc's own rule for adding prefixes/values). `vendor:` and `scenario:` are\n+  auxiliary tags documented there too. The spec delta is an **ADDED** requirement in\n+  `harness-engineering` rather than a MODIFIED \"Capability Gap Detection\", because\n+  the in-flight `add-a-judged-first-stage-to-coordinator-audit-triage` already\n+  modifies that requirement and two MODIFIED deltas on one requirement collide at\n+  archive time.\n+- `/improve-harness` needs **no source-specific code** (it aggregates arbitrary\n+  `source:` values), but its memory query is **incompatible with the live API** and\n+  must be repaired in this change, or the emitted gaps are never read:\n+  `analyze_failures.query_memory` posts no `agent_id` (required by\n+  `MemoryQueryRequest`), sends no `X-API-Key`, sends `time_window_days` (not a request\n+  field — ignored), and reads `entries` while `/memory/query` returns a `memories`\n+  list envelope. The fix: send `agent_id` (default `improve-harness`, overridable),\n+  send `Authorization: Bearer` from `COORDINATION_API_KEY` when set, read `memories` (keeping\n+  `entries`/bare-list for older coordinators), and apply the time window client-side\n+  on `created_at`. A consumer test drives `query_memory` against a local\n+  `http.server` stub that enforces the real request model and returns the real\n+  envelope with the emitter's example payload, then feeds the result through\n+  `normalize_memory_entries` / `rank_findings` and asserts `scenario-parity` appears\n+  in the source set. The SKILL.md data-sources table gains a row.\n+\n+### D4 — Nightly runner with an explicit off-switch and caps\n+\n+`agent-scenarios nightly --config <path> [--dry-run]`. Config (validated by a pydantic\n+model; JSON schema in `contracts/nightly-config.schema.json`):\n+\n+```yaml\n+enabled: false                       # off by default — must be flipped by the operator\n+disable_file: ~/.config/agent-scenarios/DISABLED   # kill-file: presence disables\n+scenarios_dir: packages/agent-scenarios/scenarios\n+repo_root: ~/agentic-coding-tools    # checkout under test (repo_sha, skills_root base)\n+skills_root: skills                  # relative to repo_root\n+vendors: [claude, codex]             # allowlist ∩ scenario.vendors; must be ≥ 2\n+vendor_commands: {claude: \"claude -p {prompt} ...\", codex: \"codex exec {prompt} ...\"}\n+env_scrub: []        # extra names only; the built-in HERMETIC_SCRUB denylist always applies (D5)\n+env_set: {}          # extra overrides; may not name a denylisted variable (D5)\n+workspaces_root: ~/.local/state/agent-scenarios/workspaces\n+retain_failed_runs: 7\n+caps:                                # every key optional; these are the defaults\n+  max_pairs: 30\n+  max_pairs_per_vendor: 15\n+  max_wall_clock_minutes: 240\n+  per_pair_timeout_seconds: 1200\n+results: {path: ~/.local/state/agent-scenarios/results.jsonl}\n+findings: {path: ~/.local/state/agent-scenarios/findings/{run_id}.json}\n+gaps: {enabled: true, spool_path: ~/.local/state/agent-scenarios/gap-spool.jsonl, agent_id: agent-scenarios-nightly,\n+       coordinator_url_env: COORDINATION_API_URL, api_key_env: COORDINATION_API_KEY}\n+judge: {enabled: false}\n+```\n+\n+Ordered guards (each writes a `run` record with the matching status and exits 0\n+unless noted):\n+\n+0. Config file missing, unparsable or schema-invalid (including a vendor in\n+   `vendors` without a `vendor_commands` entry) → message on stderr, **exit 2, no\n+   record written** (the store path itself may be unknown).\n+1. `enabled: false` → `disabled`; **no executor constructed**.\n+2. `disable_file` exists → `disabled`.\n+3. Run lock (`flock` on `<state>/nightly.lock`) held → `locked`, exit 0 (overlap is\n+   expected-benign; systemd also prevents it).\n+4. Effective vendors = `config.vendors ∩ ⋃ scenario.vendors`. Fewer than 2 →\n+   `config_error` run record, exit 2, nothing launched.\n+5. Planned pairs = Σ over scenarios of |scenario.vendors ∩ config.vendors|. If\n+   `> max_pairs` or any vendor `> max_pairs_per_vendor` → `cap_exceeded`, **exit 2,\n+   nothing launched** (fail-closed rather than silently truncating coverage).\n+6. During the run, once elapsed ≥ `max_wall_clock_minutes`, remaining pairs are not\n+   launched and are recorded `skipped_budget`; run status `budget_exhausted`.\n+\n+Pair order is deterministic (scenarios sorted by id, then vendors in config order) so\n+a budget cut drops the same tail every night and trends stay comparable.\n+\n+**Spend cap rationale**: vendor CLIs do not expose dollar cost synchronously, so the\n+cap is expressed in launched pairs, wall clock and per-pair timeout — the levers the\n+runner controls. Dollar accounting belongs to the model-usage-ledger work.\n+\n+`--dry-run` runs guard 0, then evaluates guards 1–5 **without acting on them**: it\n+prints the off-switch state (`enabled`, kill-file present), the effective vendors,\n+the planned pair list and the cap evaluation, takes no lock, writes no record of any\n+kind, constructs no executor, and exits 0 (2 when guard 0, 4 or 5 would fail). It\n+deliberately ignores `enabled: false` because the runbook's pre-enable check\n+(task 7.2) runs it while the config is still disabled.\n+\n+Exit codes, highest precedence first: 2 config/cap error; 1 one or more scenario\n+`fail` (so systemd marks the unit failed and `OnFailure=` hooks can notify); 3 no\n+`fail` but the night is not green — one or more `error` results (infrastructure\n+broken: a CLI missing, keys expired, timeouts) **or** a `budget_exhausted` run (part\n+of the matrix was never tested); 0 only for a `completed` run whose pairs all passed,\n+and for `disabled` / `locked`. An incomplete matrix therefore never looks green.\n+\n+**Workspaces**: each pair runs in `<workspaces_root>/<run_id>/<scenario_id>--<vendor>/`\n+(default `workspaces_root` = `<state>/workspaces`). Workspaces (and their sibling\n+`.origin.git`) of `pass` and `skipped_budget` pairs are deleted after scoring;\n+`fail`/`error` workspaces are kept for diagnosis. At the start of each run, run\n+directories beyond the newest `retain_failed_runs` (default 7) are deleted, so disk\n+use is bounded at ~7 × 22 workspaces.\n+\n+**Spool concurrency**: emitting to and flushing the gap spool both take an exclusive\n+`flock` on `<spool>.lock`; `flush` rewrites the spool via a temp file + `os.replace`\n+under that lock, so a manual `gaps flush` concurrent with a nightly cannot drop or\n+duplicate entries.\n+\n+The runner calls the ri-15 `run_scenario` per scenario but passes a *filtered copy*\n+of the scenario (vendors ∩ allowlist) and checks the wall-clock budget between\n+pairs. To check budget between vendors of the same scenario it iterates scenarios ×\n+vendors itself and builds each `ParityMatrix` from single-vendor runs (the runner's\n+public API is unchanged).\n+\n+### D5 — Skill-under-test materialization and sandboxing in the executor\n+\n+A broken skill change can only fail the suite if the agent actually runs the changed\n+skill. `CLIVendorExecutor` gains:\n+\n+- `skills_root: Path | None` — when set, after fixture materialization it first\n+  checks that `skills_root/<skill_under_test>/SKILL.md` exists (else an executor\n+  `error` naming the skill, no vendor launched), then copies **the whole skills\n+  tree** — every top-level directory of `skills_root`, excluding `tests/`, `.venv/`,\n+  `__pycache__/` and `node_modules/` — into `workdir/.claude/skills/` and\n+  `workdir/.agents/skills/` (the project-local skill locations the vendor CLIs read).\n+  The whole tree is required, not just the skill under test: skills resolve helpers\n+  through sibling paths (`<skill-base-dir>/../worktree/scripts/worktree.py`,\n+  `../shared/checkout_policy.py`, `../session-log/scripts/…`), so a single-skill copy\n+  would make most live runs fail for reasons unrelated to the skill. This mirrors the\n+  runtime layout `install.sh` produces. Both directories are added to the fixture's\n+  `.git/info/exclude` so they never appear in agent commits or gate checks.\n+  `skills_sha` (git HEAD of the repo containing `skills_root`, `+dirty` if modified)\n+  is recorded on every result.\n+- **Hermetic environment (fail-closed, not configurable away)** — the executor owns\n+  a built-in `HERMETIC_SCRUB` denylist that config can extend (`env_scrub`) but never\n+  shrink: GitHub tokens (`GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`,\n+  `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`); every coordinator variable that\n+  `skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/coordination_bridge.py` reads — the URL aliases\n+  `COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL`, `AGENT_COORDINATOR_API_URL`, `AGENT_COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL`,\n+  `AGENT_COORDINATOR_REST_PORT`, the API keys `COORDINATION_API_KEY`,\n+  `COORDINATOR_API_KEY`, and the Cloudflare Access service token\n+  `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` / `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET`; and `COORDINATOR_URL`, which\n+  `skills/improve-harness/scripts/analyze_failures.py` reads — plus the variables named\n+  by `gaps.api_key_env` and `gaps.coordinator_url_env`. After scrubbing and applying\n+  `env_set`, the executor **always** sets `COORDINATION_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9`\n+  (the discard port, which `_validate_url` accepts as loopback). The sentinel is\n+  needed because `coordination_bridge.py` falls back to `http://localhost:3000` when\n+  no URL variable is set — on the GX10 that *is* the live coordinator. `env_set` may\n+  not name any variable in the effective scrub set — the built-in denylist,\n+  `COORDINATION_API_URL`, any `env_scrub` entry, and the names in\n+  `gaps.api_key_env` / `gaps.coordinator_url_env` (the static part via schema\n+  `propertyNames`, the whole set by the pydantic model → guard 0, exit 2), so no\n+  valid config can re-open the live-coordinator path. Two drift tests guard the\n+  copies: `HERMETIC_SCRUB` ⊇ the bridge's `_HTTP_URL_ENV_KEYS`, `_API_KEY_ENV_KEYS` and\n+  CF variable names (skipped when the skills tree is absent), so a new bridge alias\n+  cannot silently bypass the scrub; and the config schema's\n+  `env_set.propertyNames` list equals `HERMETIC_SCRUB ∪ {COORDINATION_API_URL}`, so\n+  the schema and the executor cannot diverge. Vendor credentials (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, …) are\n+  untouched, and `HOME` is not replaced: vendor CLIs keep their auth there. MCP-based\n+  coordinator access and git transport credentials (SSH keys, credential helpers,\n+  `insteadOf` rewrites) configured under that HOME are therefore handled\n+  operationally — a dedicated nightly user/HOME with no coordinator MCP config and no\n+  GitHub push credentials (task 7.1) — and are named as a residual risk below.\n+- **`gh` shim** — the executor writes a stub `gh` executable into\n+  `<workdir>.bin/` (sibling, outside the workspace) and prepends it to the vendor's\n+  `PATH`, for every live run. It serves a deliberately small surface from a state file\n+  seeded by the fixture's optional `prs:` list: `gh auth status` (ok),\n+  `gh repo view --json`, `gh pr list|view|status --json`, `gh pr create` (records a\n+  PR whose head branch must exist on the local origin), `gh pr merge\n+  [--merge|--squash|--rebase] [--delete-branch]` (performs the merge with git against\n+  the local origin and marks the PR merged), and `gh api repos/{o}/{r}` returning\n+  `permissions.push: true` with branch protection reported absent (404). Any other\n+  invocation exits 1 and is appended to `<workdir>.bin/gh-unsupported.log`. This makes\n+  the merge-family skills runnable without GitHub, makes `pr` gates satisfiable\n+  against the local origin (the executor's post-run `gh pr view` resolves through the\n+  same shim), and guarantees no `gh` call reaches GitHub even if a credential leaks\n+  through `~/.config/gh`. **If the unsupported-call log is non-empty after the run,\n+  the verdict is forced to `error`** (\"gh shim: unsupported call …\"), so shim coverage\n+  gaps surface as infrastructure errors (exit 3, no capability gap) rather than being\n+  blamed on the skill; the shim's surface is widened by later changes as such errors\n+  appear.\n+- **Skill invocation** — copying the tree makes the skill *available*, not *used*.\n+  Every seed scenario's `task_prompt` therefore opens with an explicit invocation of\n+  its skill (`/<skill_under_test>` followed by the request), which both Claude Code\n+  and Codex resolve against the project-local skill directories; the guard test\n+  rejects a seed whose prompt does not contain `/<skill_under_test>`. Whether the\n+  agent then *follows* the skill is verified only indirectly, by gates that check the\n+  skill's distinctive artifacts (e.g. `## <Phase>` + `**Status**:` report sections,\n+  OpenSpec change layout); there is no vendor-neutral trace of skill loading. This is\n+  recorded as a residual risk and the live broken-skill drill (task 7.5) is the\n+  end-to-end check.\n+- `timeout_seconds` is fed from `caps.per_pair_timeout_seconds`, and a\n+  `TimeoutExpired` now yields an error message `vendor CLI timed out after <N>s`\n+  distinct from `vendor CLI unavailable` (today both return exit 127 with the same\n+  message, which would make the runbook's triage impossible).\n+\n+`FixtureSpec` gains `local_remote: bool = false`: create a bare repo at\n+`<workdir>.origin.git` (sibling, outside the workspace), `git remote add origin`, and\n+push the base branch; and `prs: list[{number, head, base, title}] = []`, the seed\n+state for the `gh` shim (head branches are pushed to the local origin at\n+materialization). Push/merge skills then operate against a local origin and never\n+reach GitHub. Gates for these scenarios use `command` checks such as\n+`git ls-remote origin <branch>` or `git -C ... merge-base --is-ancestor`.\n+\n+These are model/executor extensions with backward-compatible defaults; existing\n+scenarios and tests are unaffected.\n+\n+### D6 — Seed suite composition and self-test\n+\n+Skill families (constant `SKILL_FAMILIES` in `suite.py`; unknown skills map to\n+`other`, which does not count toward coverage):\n+\n+| Family | Skills |\n+|---|---|\n+| plan | `plan-feature`, `iterate-on-plan` |\n+| implement | `implement-feature`, `iterate-on-implementation` |\n+| validate | `validate-feature` |\n+| merge | `merge-pull-requests`, `cleanup-feature` |\n+\n+Suite (11 scenarios, all with `vendors: [claude, codex]` at minimum):\n+\n+| # | Scenario id | Skill | Discriminating gates (sketch) |\n+|---|---|---|---|\n+| 1 | `plan-feature-basic` (existing) | plan-feature | proposal/tasks exist on change branch; Mitigation: stable gap keys so `/improve-harness` ranks by\n+  frequency; `trend` shows rates, not single results.\n+- **Skill invocation vs. skill following** — the prompt invokes the skill, but no\n+  vendor-neutral signal proves the agent followed it; gates check the skill's\n+  artifacts instead (D5). A vendor that ignores the skill yet produces equivalent\n+  artifacts passes. Mitigation: skill-distinctive gates and the live broken-skill\n+  drill (task 7.5).\n+- **HOME-scoped credentials** — vendor CLIs need the nightly user's HOME, so MCP\n+  coordinator config and git push credentials there are outside the executor's\n+  control. Mitigation: dedicated nightly user/HOME (task 7.1, runbook check).\n+- **Skill materialization fidelity** — vendor CLIs may also load user-global skills\n+  (`~/.claude/skills`), shadowing or supplementing the project copy. Runbook\n+  instructs running the nightly under a dedicated user/HOME with no global skills;\n+  `skills_sha` makes attribution explicit.\n+- **Store locality** — trends are only queryable on the host that owns the file.\n+  Accepted (single GX10 host); `ResultsStore` seam allows a coordinator backend.\n+- **`gh` shim fidelity** — the shim is not GitHub; a skill that works against the\n+  shim may still break against real GitHub (and vice versa). Accepted: the suite\n+  measures skill *behaviour* (did it merge the right branch, keep history, archive the\n+  change), not GitHub API compatibility; unsupported calls are surfaced as `error`\n+  so the gap list stays clean.\n+- **Standalone-tier only** — scenario agents never see a coordinator, so coordinated\n+  -tier code paths are not exercised by this suite. Accepted for hermeticity; a\n+  coordinator-in-fixture mode is future work.\n+- **New tag vocabulary value** — consumers that enumerate sources (export of shared\n+  learnings, skill-audit evidence join) will see a new value; they treat `source:` as\n+  open-ended today (verified in `analyze_failures.rank_findings`). Shared-learnings\n+  export keeps its own allowlist of prefixes, which includes `source:`.\n+\n+## Testing strategy\n+\n+- All unit/integration tests use `FakeExecutor` (or a test subclass); no vendor CLI,\n+  no network: `CoordinatorMemorySink` is tested against a local\n+  `http.server` stub; It deliberately stopped short of\n+the parts that make the harness *pay off* (its `tasks.md` §10 defers them here):\n+\n+- **Coverage** — only two seed scenarios exist (`plan-feature-basic`,\n+  `implement-feature-basic`); nothing exercises validate or merge skills.\n+- **Cadence** — `python -m agent_scenarios` is a lister/validator. There is no\n+  command that runs the suite end-to-end, no schedule, and no guard rails\n+  (off-switch, spend/size cap) that an unattended nightly run needs.\n+- **Feedback** — findings are written to a JSON file that nobody reads. The\n+  `/improve-harness` capability-gap pipeline never sees a scenario failure, so a skill\n+  regression caught by the harness does not become an improvement signal.\n+- **Trend** — a parity matrix is produced and discarded. There is no way to ask\n+  \"how has `validate-feature` been doing on `codex` over the last two weeks?\", which\n+  is the signal the roadmap wants to eventually gate dispatcher routing on.\n+- **Sensitivity to skill changes** — the live executor runs a vendor CLI in a bare\n+  fixture repo; nothing puts the *skill under test* (from the checkout being\n+  evaluated) into that workspace, so a broken skill change would not reliably show up\n+  in the suite at all.\n+\n+## What Changes\n+\n+1. **Seed suite (11 scenarios)** — 9 new scenarios plus the 2 existing ones, covering\n+   the four skill families: plan (3), implement (3), validate (3), merge (2). Every\n+   scenario declares at least 2 vendors. Each scenario ships with a scripted *golden*\n+   and *broken* `FakeExecutor` outcome so the test suite proves its gates are both\n+   satisfiable and discriminating. A suite-coverage guard test enforces the ≥10 /\n+   all-four-families / ≥2-vendors floor. `implement-feature-basic` is revised to gate\n+   on a push to a local bare `origin` instead of a real GitHub PR.\n+2. **Harness extensions for live runs** — fixture `local_remote` (a sibling bare repo\n+   wired as `origin`, so push/merge skills never touch GitHub) with seeded `prs:`; a\n+   small `gh` shim on every live run's `PATH` backed by that local origin, so the\n+   merge-family skills (which require `gh`) run without GitHub and unsupported `gh`\n+   calls surface as infrastructure errors; materialization of the **whole skills\n+   tree** from a configurable `skills_root` (skills reference siblings via\n+   `<skill-base-dir>/../`) into the workspace's `.claude/skills/` and\n+   `.agents/skills/`; and a hermetic vendor environment — GitHub and coordinator\n+   credentials and every coordinator address/credential variable scrubbed by a\n+   built-in denylist that config can extend but not shrink, `COORDINATION_API_URL`\n+   forced to an unreachable sentinel so fixture agents run standalone and never write\n+   to the live coordinator; every seed prompt explicitly invokes its skill under test;\n+   a timeout reported distinctly from a missing CLI.\n+3. **Durable results store + query CLI** — an append-only, schema-versioned JSONL\n+   store (one record per run × scenario × vendor, plus a run-summary record) and\n+   `agent-scenarios results {query,trend,latest}` filtering by vendor, skill, skill\n+   family, scenario and time window.\n+4. **Capability-gap emission** — each deterministic scenario *failure* (not an\n+   executor/infra error) becomes an episodic-memory entry using the shared D4 tag\n+   schema with a new `source:scenario-parity` value, written through the coordinator\n+   `POST /memory/store` path with an offline JSONL spool fallback and a `gaps flush`\n+   replay command. `/improve-harness` needs no source-specific code, but its memory\n+   query is repaired to match the live `POST /memory/query` contract (`agent_id`, API\n+   key, `memories` envelope) — today it would never read the emitted gaps; the new\n+   source value is documented in the memory conventions and tag-convention tests.\n+5. **Nightly runner** — `agent-scenarios nightly --config <file>` orchestrating: spool\n+   flush → suite load → vendor allowlist → cap check → run → results append →\n+   findings file → capability gaps. Explicit off-switch (config `enabled: false` by\n+   default *and* a kill-file), per-run size/spend caps (max scenario×vendor pairs,\n+   max pairs per vendor, wall-clock budget, per-pair timeout), a run lock against\n+   overlapping runs, incremental result appends (a killed run keeps its completed\n+   pairs), bounded workspace retention, a `--dry-run` that works while still disabled,\n+   and exit codes that distinguish skill failures (1) from a non-green night without\n+   skill failures — infrastructure errors or a budget-exhausted, incomplete matrix\n+   (3) — and config/cap errors (2).\n+6. **Deploy templates, not deployments** — systemd user `.service`/`.timer`\n+   *templates* and an example config under `packages/agent-scenarios/deploy/`, plus a\n+   runbook. Nothing is installed or enabled by this change.\n+\n+### Out of scope\n+\n+- **Incident auto-seeding** (auto-rollback / ESCALATE / holdout failure → draft\n+  scenario) — roadmap item ri-17, `auto-seed-scenarios-from-incidents`.\n+- **Dispatcher routing gate** on parity results (\"skill changes must pass the parity\n+  suite before the dispatcher routes real work through them\") — this change provides\n+  the queryable signal (`results latest`) but does not wire any gate.\n+- Installing/enabling the timer on the GX10, and the first live nightly run — operator\n+  tasks, listed unchecked in `tasks.md`.\n+- Running paid vendor matrices during implementation or CI — all tests use\n+  `FakeExecutor`.\n+- Any change to trust posture (`TRUST_POSTURE.md`).\n+\n+## Approaches Considered\n+\n+### Approach 1: Package-local nightly runner + JSONL results store + memory-path gaps (Recommended)\n+\n+Everything lives in `packages/agent-scenarios/`: a `nightly` subcommand driven by a\n+YAML config, an append-only JSONL results store with a query CLI, and a gap emitter\n+that writes D4-tagged entries via the coordinator HTTP memory API (spool on failure).\n+Scheduling is a systemd user timer template.\n+\n+- **Pros**: no DB migration and no coordinator change; run history visible in the Actions UI.\n+- **Cons**: needs vendor CLI credentials in CI secrets (trust-posture change);\n+  hosted runners lack the GX10 vendor setup; artifact retention is time-boxed and not\n+  queryable; self-hosted GX10 runners (the roadmap's CI-migration item) are not in place yet.\n+- **Effort**: M\n+\n+### Selected Approach\n+\n+**Approach 1** (autonomous planning, recorded in `design.md` → \"Assumptions\n+(autonomous planning)\"). It satisfies \"queryable per vendor per skill over time\" with\n+the simplest durable store, avoids a DB migration and any trust-posture change, and\n+keeps every moving part testable in-container. The store is behind a small\n+`ResultsStore` interface so a later change can add a coordinator-backed implementation\n+(Approach 2) if a cross-host consumer (operator status surface, dispatcher gate)\n+materialises; the JSONL file would then become its import source. Approach 3 is\n+rejected primarily on trust posture (vendor keys in CI).\n+\n+## Impact\n+\n+- **Code**: `packages/agent-scenarios/` (new modules `suite.py`, `materialize.py`,\n+  `gh_shim.py`, coverage floor\n+\n+The agent-scenarios package SHALL ship a seed suite of at least 10 scenarios covering the plan, implement, validate and merge skill families, with at least 2 scenarios per family and at least 2 declared vendors per scenario, every scenario's task prompt SHALL explicitly invoke its skill under test, and a guard test SHALL fail the build when the suite drops below this floor.\n+\n+#### Scenario: the shipped suite meets the coverage floor\n+- **WHEN** the guard test loads every `*.scenario.yaml` under `packages/agent-scenarios/scenarios/`\n+- **THEN** it SHALL find at least 10 scenarios with unique ids\n+- **AND** each of the families plan, implement, validate and merge SHALL be represented by at least 2 scenarios according to the package's skill-family map\n+- **AND** every scenario SHALL declare at least 2 vendors\n+- **AND** every scenario's `task_prompt` SHALL contain `/<skill_under_test>`\n+\n+#### Scenario: a seed prompt that does not invoke its skill fails the guard\n+- **WHEN** the guard test finds a seed scenario whose `task_prompt` does not contain `/<skill_under_test>`\n+- **THEN** the guard test SHALL fail and name the scenario id\n+\n+#### Scenario: removing scenarios below the floor fails the guard\n+- **WHEN** the guard test runs against a suite directory containing only 9 scenarios, or with no merge-family scenario\n+- **THEN** the guard test SHALL fail and name the unmet floor\n+\n+### Requirement: Seed scenarios are self-tested as satisfiable and discriminating\n+\n+Every seed scenario SHALL have a scripted golden outcome and a scripted broken outcome for the fake executor, and the test suite MUST show that the golden outcome passes all goal gates while the broken outcome fails at least one named gate.\n+\n+#### Scenario: golden outcome passes every gate\n+- **WHEN** a seed scenario is run through the runner with the fake executor scripted with its golden outcome\n+- **THEN** every vendor result SHALL have deterministic status `pass`\n+\n+#### Scenario: broken outcome fails a named gate\n+- **WHEN** the same scenario is run with its broken outcome\n+- **THEN** every vendor result SHALL have deterministic status `fail`\n+- **AND** the failed gate ids SHALL include the gate id named by the broken outcome\n+\n+#### Scenario: a seed scenario without outcomes is rejected\n+- **WHEN** a scenario file is added without a corresponding golden/broken outcome module\n+- **THEN** the guard test SHALL fail and name the scenario id\n+\n+### Requirement: Live runs never reach real GitHub\n+\n+Seed scenarios SHALL NOT depend on GitHub side effects. Push and merge behaviour MUST be exercised against a fixture-local bare `origin` repository, every live run SHALL resolve `gh` to a local shim instead of the real GitHub CLI, and the live executor SHALL always remove a built-in denylist of GitHub and coordinator credential and address variables from the vendor subprocess environment and point skill coordinator detection at an unreachable address; configuration MAY extend the denylist but MUST NOT remove from it or override the unreachable address.\n+\n+#### Scenario: local remote fixture\n+- **WHEN** a scenario fixture sets `local_remote: true`\n+- **THEN** fixture materialization SHALL create a bare repository outside the workspace, register it as `origin`, and push the base branch to it\n+\n+#### Scenario: PR gates require a local remote\n+- **WHEN** the guard test finds a seed scenario with a `pr` goal gate and `local_remote` not set\n+- **THEN** the guard test SHALL fail\n+\n+#### Scenario: credential variables are scrubbed\n+- **WHEN** the live executor runs a vendor command with an empty `env_scrub` while `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `COORDINATOR_API_KEY`, `COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL`, `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` and `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` are set in the runner's environment\n+- **THEN** none of those variables SHALL be present in the vendor subprocess environment\n+\n+#### Scenario: config cannot re-open the live coordinator path\n+- **WHEN** a nightly config sets `env_set` with a key `COORDINATION_API_URL`, `COORDINATOR_URL`, any other built-in denylisted variable, any `env_scrub` entry, or the name configured in `gaps.api_key_env` or `gaps.coordinator_url_env`\n+- **THEN** the config SHALL be rejected as invalid (exit 2, no record written)\n+- **AND** for any valid config, `COORDINATION_API_URL` in the vendor subprocess environment SHALL equal `http://127.0.0.1:9`\n+\n+#### Scenario: the denylist covers every coordinator variable the skills read\n+- **WHEN** the drift test compares the built-in denylist with the URL, API-key and Cloudflare Access variable names read by `skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/coordination_bridge.py`\n+- **THEN** every such name SHALL be in the denylist\n+\n+#### Scenario: the runner's coordinator credential never reaches an agent\n+- **WHEN** the live executor runs a vendor command while the variable named by `gaps.api_key_env` is set in the runner's environment, even if `env_scrub` omits it\n+- **THEN** that variable SHALL NOT be present in the vendor subprocess environment\n+- **AND** `COORDINATION_API_URL` in the vendor subprocess environment SHALL equal `http://127.0.0.1:9`\n+\n+#### Scenario: gh resolves to the shim\n+- **WHEN** a live run executes and the vendor command invokes `gh pr merge <n> --squash` for a PR seeded in the fixture's `prs` list\n+- **THEN** the `gh` executable found first on the vendor's `PATH` SHALL be the shim outside the workspace\n+- **AND** the PR head SHALL be merged into the base branch of the local `origin` and the PR SHALL be reported as merged by a subsequent `gh pr view <n> --json state`\n+\n+#### Scenario: an unsupported gh call is an infrastructure error\n+- **WHEN** the agent invokes a `gh` subcommand the shim does not implement\n+- **THEN** the shim SHALL exit 1 and log the call\n+- **AND** the pair's deterministic status SHALL be `error` with a message naming the unsupported call, and no capability-gap entry SHALL be emitted for it\n+\n+### Requirement: Skill under test is materialized from the checkout being evaluated\n+\n+When a skills root is configured, the live executor SHALL verify that the scenario's skill under test exists in that root, copy the whole skills tree (excluding test, virtual-environment and cache directories) into the workspace's project-local skill directories before running the vendor, and SHALL record the skills revision on each result.\n+\n+#### Scenario: skill copied into the workspace\n+- **WHEN** the executor runs a scenario whose `skill_under_test` is `validate-feature` with `skills_root` set\n+- **THEN** `.claude/skills/validate-feature/` and `.agents/skills/validate-feature/` SHALL exist in the workspace with the contents of `skills_root/validate-feature/`\n+- **AND** sibling skills such as `.claude/skills/worktree/` SHALL also exist, so `<skill-base-dir>/../<sibling>/` references resolve\n+- **AND** no `tests/` or `.venv/` directory from `skills_root` SHALL be copied\n+- **AND** those paths SHALL be excluded from git in the workspace so they never appear in agent commits\n+- **AND** the resulting `result` record SHALL carry `skills_sha` equal to the git HEAD of the repository containing `skills_root`, suffixed `+dirty` when that checkout has uncommitted changes\n+\n+#### Scenario: missing skill is an executor error\n+- **WHEN** `skills_root` does not contain the scenario's skill under test\n+- **THEN** the run SHALL produce deterministic status `error` with a message naming the missing skill\n+- **AND** no vendor command SHALL be executed\n+\n+#### Scenario: a timeout is distinguishable from a missing CLI\n+- **WHEN** the vendor command exceeds the per-pair timeout\n+- **THEN** the result SHALL have deterministic status `error` with a message stating the timeout in seconds, distinct from the message for an unavailable CLI\n+\n+### Requirement: Durable per-vendor per-skill results store\n+\n+Each nightly run SHALL append one schema-versioned result record per scenario and vendor, and one run-summary record, to an append-only results store, and the package SHALL provide a query interface that filters and aggregates results by vendor, skill, skill family, scenario and time window.\n+\n+#### Scenario: results are appended per scenario and vendor\n+- **WHEN** a nightly run executes 11 scenarios across 2 vendors\n+- **THEN** the store SHALL gain 22 `result` records and 1 `run` record sharing one `run_id`\n+- **AND** each `result` record SHALL include `scenario_id`, `skill_under_test`, `skill_family`, `vendor`, `deterministic_status`, `failed_gates`, `trajectory_status`, `duration_seconds`, `repo_sha`, `skills_sha`, `error`, `recorded_at` and `schema_version`, with nullable fields present as explicit null\n+\n+#### Scenario: query by vendor and skill over a time window\n+- **WHEN** an operator runs `agent-scenarios results query --vendor codex --skill validate-feature --since <date>`\n+- **THEN** only `result` records matching that vendor, skill and window SHALL be returned\n+\n+#### Scenario: query by skill family and scenario\n+- **WHEN** an operator runs `agent-scenarios results query --family validate` or `agent-scenarios results query --scenario validate-feature-clean-pass --until <date>`\n+- **THEN** only `result` records whose `skill_family` (respectively `scenario_id` and `recorded_at` window) match SHALL be returned\n+\n+#### Scenario: trend aggregates pass rate per bucket\n+- **WHEN** an operator runs `agent-scenarios results trend --group-by vendor,skill --bucket day`\n+- **THEN** the output SHALL report, per vendor, skill and day, the pass count, fail count, error count and a pass rate whose denominator excludes `error` and `skipped_budget` results\n+\n+#### Scenario: reader tolerates a torn final line and unknown versions\n+- **WHEN** the store ends with a partial line or contains a record with an unknown `schema_version`\n+- **THEN** the reader SHALL skip those lines with a warning and return all valid records\n+\n+#### Scenario: results survive an interrupted run\n+- **WHEN** a nightly run is killed after 5 of its planned pairs have been scored\n+- **THEN** the store SHALL contain those 5 `result` records and no `run` record for that `run_id`\n+- **AND** `results query` SHALL return them marked as belonging to an interrupted run\n+\n+#### Scenario: a run in progress is not reported as interrupted\n+- **WHEN** `results query` runs while a nightly run holds the run lock and has appended result records but no `run` record yet\n+- **THEN** those records SHALL be marked as belonging to **THEN** exactly one record per (scenario, vendor) SHALL be returned, the most recent by `recorded_at`\n+\n+### Requirement: Scenario failures feed the capability-gap pipeline\n+\n+Every deterministic scenario failure SHALL be emitted as a capability-gap episodic-memory entry using the shared tag schema with `source:scenario-parity`, and entries that cannot be delivered to the coordinator MUST be spooled locally and replayed on a later run. Executor errors, budget skips and LLM-judge findings SHALL NOT produce capability-gap entries.\n+\n+#### Scenario: a failing gate produces a tagged gap entry\n+- **WHEN** a result has deterministic status `fail` for scenario `validate-feature-clean-pass` on vendor `codex` with failed gate `report-has-status`\n+- **THEN** the emitter SHALL send one entry whose `capability_gap:` tag names the first failed gate in scenario declaration order, with tags including `capability_gap`, `capability_gap:scenario-parity/validate-feature-clean-pass/report-has-status`, `failure_type:verification_failed`, `affected_skill:validate-feature`, `severity:high`, `source:scenario-parity` and `vendor:codex`\n+- **AND** the entry's `session_id` SHALL be the nightly `run_id`\n+\n+#### Scenario: errors and judge findings do not emit gaps\n+- **WHEN** a result has deterministic status `error` or `skipped_budget`, or passes gates but carries LLM-judge findings\n+- **THEN** no capability-gap entry SHALL be emitted for it\n+\n+#### Scenario: coordinator unreachable spools entries\n+- **WHEN** the coordinator memory endpoint is unreachable during emission\n+- **THEN** every entry SHALL be appended to the gap spool file and none SHALL be lost\n+\n+#### Scenario: spool replay\n+- **WHEN** `agent-scenarios gaps flush` runs and the coordinator is reachable\n+- **THEN** spooled entries SHALL be delivered and removed from the spool\n+- **AND** entries that still fail delivery SHALL remain in the spool\n+\n+#### Scenario: an application-level rejection is not a delivery\n+- **WHEN** the coordinator memory endpoint answers HTTP 200 with `success: false`, a non-JSON body, or a non-2xx status\n+- **THEN** the entry SHALL be treated as undelivered: spooled on emission and kept in the spool on flush\n+\n+#### Scenario: no coordinator URL configured spools instead of guessing\n+- **WHEN** the variable named by `gaps.coordinator_url_env` is unset\n+- **THEN** every entry SHALL be spooled and no HTTP request SHALL be made to any host\n+\n+#### Scenario: concurrent flush and emission lose nothing\n+- **WHEN** `agent-scenarios gaps flush` and a nightly emission touch the spool concurrently\n+- **THEN** after both finish, every entry SHALL be either delivered or present exactly once in the spool\n+\n+#### Scenario: a deliberately broken skill change produces a capability gap\n+- **WHEN** the suite runs against a skills root in which a skill under test has been deliberately broken so that its scenario's gates fail\n+- **THEN** the run SHALL record a `fail` result for that scenario\n+- **AND** a capability-gap entry with `affected_skill` equal to that skill and `source:scenario-parity` SHALL be emitted\n+- **AND** `/improve-harness` failure analysis over that entry SHALL rank a finding for that capability gap with `scenario-parity` in its source set\n+\n+### Requirement: Nightly runner with off-switch and spend caps\n+\n+The package SHALL provide a nightly command that runs the suite across an allowlist of at least 2 vendors under explicit size and time caps, and that does nothing unless explicitly enabled.\n+\n+#### Scenario: disabled by default\n+- **WHEN** `agent-scenarios nightly` runs with a config whose `enabled` is false\n+- **THEN** no executor SHALL be constructed and no vendor command SHALL run\n+- **AND** a `run` record with status `disabled` SHALL be appended and the command SHALL exit 0\n+\n+#### Scenario: kill-file disables an enabled config\n+- **WHEN** the config is enabled and the configured `disable_file` exists\n+- **THEN** the run SHALL behave as disabled\n+\n+#### Scenario: over-cap plan refuses to start\n+- **WHEN** the planned scenario×vendor pairs exceed `caps.max_pairs`, or any vendor's pairs exceed `caps.max_pairs_per_vendor`\n+- **THEN** no pair SHALL be launched\n+- **AND** a `run` record with status `cap_exceeded` SHALL be appended and the command SHALL exit 2\n+\n+#### Scenario: wall-clock budget stops launching new pairs\n+- **WHEN** elapsed run time reaches `caps.max_wall_clock_minutes` with pairs remaining\n+- **THEN** remaining pairs SHALL NOT be launched and SHALL be recorded with status `skipped_budget`\n+- **AND** the `run` record status SHALL be `budget_exhausted`\n+- **AND** when no executed pair has status `fail`, the command SHALL exit 3, never 0\n+\n+#### Scenario: fewer than two effective vendors is a config error\n+- **WHEN** the vendor allowlist intersected with the suite's declared vendors yields fewer than 2 vendors\n+- **THEN** the command SHALL exit 2 without launching any pair\n+- **AND** a `run` record with status `config_error` SHALL be appended\n+\n+#### Scenario: invalid config writes nothing\n+- **WHEN** the config file is unparsable, violates the config schema, or lists a vendor without a `vendor_commands` entry\n+- **THEN** the command SHALL exit 2 with a message naming the problem, launch no pair and write no record\n+\n+#### Scenario: overlapping runs are refused\n+- **WHEN** a nightly run starts while another holds the run lock\n+- **THEN** it SHALL record status `locked` and exit 0 without launching any pair\n+\n+#### Scenario: dry run plans without executing\n+- **WHEN** `agent-scenarios nightly --dry-run` runs with a valid config, whether `enabled` is true or false\n+- **THEN** it SHALL print the off-switch state, the effective vendors, the planned pairs and the cap evaluation\n+- **AND** it SHALL NOT construct an executor, take the run lock, launch any pair or write any record\n+\n+#### Scenario: failing scenarios make the run exit non-zero\n+- **WHEN** a completed nightly run has at least one `fail` result\n+- **THEN** the command SHALL exit 1 after writing results, findings and gaps, whether or not the wall-clock budget was exhausted\n+\n+#### Scenario: an infrastructure-only failure is not a green night\n+- **WHEN** a nightly run has no `fail` result but at least one `error` result or the run status `budget_exhausted`\n+- **THEN** the command SHALL exit 3\n+- **AND** no capability-gap entry SHALL be emitted for the `error` results\n+\n+#### Scenario: workspaces are bounded\n+- **WHEN** a nightly run finishes\n+- **THEN** the workspaces of its `pass` pairs SHALL have been deleted and those of its `fail` and `error` pairs SHALL remain\n+- **AND** at the start of the next run, run directories older than the newest `retain_failed_runs` SHALL be deleted\n+\n+### Requirement: Schedule shipped as templates only\n+\n+The change SHALL ship the nightly schedule only as systemd unit and timer templates plus an example config with `enabled: false`, and MUST NOT install, enable or start any scheduled job.\n+\n+#### Scenario: templates and example config are it\n+\n+#### Scenario: scenario-parity entries are retrievable by the improve-harness memory query\n+- **WHEN** a scenario-parity entry is stored through the coordinator memory API\n+- **THEN** it API\n+- **WHEN** `/improve-harness` queries `POST /memory/query` against a coordinator that requires `agent_id` and an API key and answers with a `memories` list envelope\n+- **THEN** the request SHALL include `agent_id` and, when `COORDINATION_API_KEY` is set, an `Authorization: Bearer` header\n+- **AND** the entries in the `memories` list SHALL be returned to failure analysis\n+- **AND** The run\n+executes the seed scenario suite across a vendor allowlist (default `claude` + `codex`),\n+appends results to a durable store, writes review findings, and emits capability gaps\n+(`source:scenario-parity`) that `/improve-harness` reads. It is **off by default** and ships\n+only as templates: nothing in the repository installs, enables or starts a schedule.\n+\n+## Install (operator, once)\n+\n+1. Create a **dedicated nightly user/HOME** on the host. It must have: no user-global skills\n+   (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`), no coordinator MCP configuration, and no GitHub\n+   push credentials (SSH keys, credential helpers, `insteadOf` rewrites). Vendor CLIs keep\n+   their own auth under that HOME, so these are controlled operationally; the executor\n+   cannot replace HOME. Install the `claude` and `codex` CLIs and their keys for that user.\n+2. Copy `packages/agent-scenarios/deploy/nightly.example.yaml` to\n+   `~/.config/agent-scenarios/nightly.yaml`, fill `vendor_commands` and the paths, and keep\n+   `enabled: false`.\n+3. Review the plan: `agent-scenarios nightly --dry-run`. It prints the off-switch state, the\n+   effective vendors, the planned (scenario, vendor) pairs and the cap evaluation; it takes no\n+   lock, writes no record and starts no vendor (it works with `enabled: false`).\n+4. Render the unit and timer from `deploy/systemd/*.template` (replace `@UV@` and `@REPO@`),\n+   place them in `~/.config/systemd/user/`, run `systemctl --user daemon-reload`. Keep\n+   `TimeoutStartSec` at or above `max_wall_clock_minutes + per_pair_timeout_seconds + 10 min`\n+   (default 270 min): the budget is only checked between pairs.\n+5. Flip `enabled: true`, run the service once by hand, review results/findings/gaps, then\n+   `systemctl --user enable --now agent-scenarios-nightly.timer`.\n+\n+## Disable (any one of)\n+\n+- `systemctl --user disable --now agent-scenarios-nightly.timer`\n+- create the kill-file (`disable_file`, default `~/.config/agent-scenarios/DISABLED`)\n+- set `enabled: false`\n+\n+A disabled run appends a `disabled` run record, constructs no executor and exits 0.\n+\n+## Exit codes and triage\n+\n+| Code | Meaning | First action |\n+|------|---------|--------------|\n+| 0 | `completed`, every pair passed (also `disabled` / `locked`) | none |\n+| 1 | one or more scenarios `fail` | `results query --status fail`; a capability gap was emitted per failing (scenario, vendor) |\n+| 2 | config or cap error (invalid config writes **no** record; `cap_exceeded`, `config_error` write one) | fix the config or raise the cap deliberately; nothing was launched |\n+| 3 | no `fail`, but one or more `error` results (a CLI missing, expired keys, timeouts, an unsupported `gh` call) **or** an incomplete matrix (`budget_exhausted`) | read the `error` text in `results query --status error`; no capability gap is emitted for infrastructure errors |\n+\n+Precedence: 2 > 1 > 3 > 0. Systemd marks the unit failed for 1, 2 and 3 (`SuccessExitStatus=0`).\n+Error texts: `vendor CLI timed out after Ns` (raise `per_pair_timeout_seconds` or investigate\n+the scenario) is distinct from `vendor CLI unavailable` (binary missing);\n+`gh shim: unsupported call ...` means the agent used a `gh` subcommand the local shim does\n+not implement (widen the shim in a follow-up change; it is not a skill failure).\n+\n+## Hermetic live runs\n+\n+Each pair runs in `<workspaces_root>/<run_id>/<scenario>--<vendor>/` against a fixture-local\n+bare `origin` (`<workspace>.origin.git`). `gh` resolves to a local shim (`<workspace>.bin/gh`)\n+so no call reaches GitHub. The vendor subprocess never sees GitHub tokens, any coordinator\n+URL / API key / Cloudflare Access variable, or the variables named by `gaps.api_key_env` /\n+`gaps.coordinator_url_env`, and `COORDINATION_API_URL` is forced to `http://127.0.0.1:9`.\n+`env_scrub` can only add to that denylist and `env_set` may not name any scrubbed variable.\n+The whole `skills/` tree of the checkout under test is copied into the workspace's\n+`.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` (excluded from git) and `skills_sha` (`+dirty` when\n+modified) is recorded on every result.\n+\n+## Workspaces and retention\n+\n+Workspaces of `pass` and `skipped_budget` pairs are deleted after scoring; `fail` and `error`\n+workspaces (and their `.origin.git`) are kept for diagnosis. At the start of each run, run\n+directories beyond the newest `retain_failed_runs` (default 7) are deleted.\n+\n+## Results\n+\n+```\n+agent-scenarios results query  --vendor codex --skill validate-feature --since 2026-10-01\n+agent-scenarios results query  --family merge --status fail --format table\n+agent-scenarios results trend  --group-by vendor,skill --bucket week\n+agent-scenarios results latest --skill implement-feature\n+```\n+\n+Records are appended as each pair is scored, so a killed run keeps its completed pairs; a\n+`result` whose `run_id` has no `run` record is reported as `interrupted` (or `in_progress`\n+while the run lock is held). Trend pass rate is `pass / (pass + fail)`; `error` and\n+`skipped_budget` are counted separately.\n+\n+## Capability gaps and /improve-harness\n+\n+Each deterministic `fail` becomes one memory entry tagged `source:scenario-parity` (see\n+`docs/guides/memory-conventions.md`). Undeliverable entries are spooled to `gap-spool.jsonl`\n+and replayed at the start of the next run or by `agent-scenarios gaps flush`; delivery counts\n+only on HTTP 2xx with `success: true`, and an unset URL variable spools without any request.\n+\n+- **Frequency unit**: `/improve-harness` counts raw memory entries, so a finding's frequency\n+  is the number of failing **(run, vendor) pairs**, not nights.\n+- **Two URL variables, one coordinator**: the gap emitter reads `COORDINATION_API_URL`\n+  (default; configurable via `gaps.coordinator_url_env`) and `COORDINATION_API_KEY`, whereas\n+  `/improve-harness` reads `COORDINATOR_URL`.
